content.comment_body: Hello! I'm attempting to download software from a [product_name] controller installed by an unknown contractor when my parents' house was built. After switching the [product_name] (article_no: [article_no]) to programming mode, I managed to connect to the device, but when trying to transfer the software from [product_name] to my computer (WIN10), I receive an error message (see attachment). Can anyone assist with resolving this issue? I'm using [product_name] engineering software [version_no] and connecting between [product_name] and PC with a dedicated cable. Appreciate any help!
Are you referring to 'transfer mode' when you say 'programming mode'?
Yes, the manual refers to it as 'programming mode'.

If you're using Windows 10, you likely have a USB interface rather than RS232. I assume you have the [product_name] USB cable. If that's the case, have you installed the appropriate driver for this cable? The driver sets up a virtual RS232 interface, which you need to choose as the correct COM port in the transfer window when using the cable.
I've checked the manual, and 'programming mode' is not the correct setting. You need to use 'transfer mode' (PC->[product_name]). Refer to the attachment for guidance.
That's the mode I successfully used to connect to the controller. The display showed PC --> [product_name], and in the engineering software I selected [product_name] -> PC.
Have you configured the correct settings in the transfer window? For me, it's COM6, which is the virtual interface created by my cable's driver.
On my setup, the program automatically detects the cable connected. My laptop only reports two COM ports: COM6 and COM7.

COM ports are not directly USB ports. The driver used with the USB cable sets up a virtual COM interface. Plugging the cable into one USB port might create COM6, using the other could create COM7. For me, it's COM6 (see attachment).
Please verify in the device manager that the COM interface settings are correct for your connection.
That matches what I see on my system as well.
I also downloaded a driver shared in an earlier thread regarding connection issues with the controller.
You haven't answered my previous question. I asked if you're using a [company_name] USB cable. If so, there's a dedicated driver for Windows 10.
Yes, I have the [company_name] [product_name] USB cable.

Visit the website: CP210x USB to UART Bridge VCP Drivers - Silicon Labs (silabs.com) ([url]). Select 'Downloads' and choose the driver: CP210x Universal Windows Driver v[version_no] [document]. This driver supports Windows 10.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter challenges transferring a program from a [product_name] controller to their PC, stemming from unclear terminology related to operating and transfer modes, confusion over how virtual COM ports work with USB cable drivers, and difficulties with the configuration process. The interface and procedure are not intuitive, leading to frequent mistakes when setting up the connection between the controller and the PC.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope for a straightforward and reliable process to download programs from the [product_name] module to their PC, without confusion over transfer modes, COM ports, or the need for manual driver installation.
